headline: Google shields Android from scammers with new AI and screen sharing protections
summary: Google is rolling out advanced AI-powered scam detection for Messages and enhanced screen sharing privacy to protect users from sophisticated fraud attempts.
details: Google has announced a suite of new security features for Android, aiming to bolster defenses against increasingly sophisticated scams. The company is introducing an optional Enhanced Protection mode for Google Messages, which utilizes cloud-based Gemini models for advanced threat detection without compromising user privacy.

Link protection in Google Messages is also getting an upgrade. Gemini Nano will now work with real-time web signals to verify the trustworthiness of unfamiliar links, helping users avoid malicious websites before they even click. Scam warnings will also be expanded beyond Pixel phones to hundreds of millions of additional Android devices, appearing directly in the notification shade.

A significant enhancement is improved protection during screen sharing. Sensitive information like login credentials and payment details will now be automatically hidden when sharing your screen across Chrome and Android WebView. This aims to thwart scammers who trick users into sharing their screens to steal personal data.

Further bolstering security, Android is implementing improved call-forwarding protection. It will prevent apps from silently enabling call forwarding and will display proactive warnings if a user is tricked into manually entering codes to enable it, stopping scammers from intercepting calls and one-time passcodes.

headline_marked: Colossal Biosciences [[launches AI platform]] to accelerate de-extinction
headline: Colossal Biosciences launches AI platform to accelerate de-extinction
summary: GenoMorph uses AI to identify genes for de-extinction projects, starting with the dodo bird.
details: Colossal Biosciences has unveiled GenoMorph, a new AI platform designed to speed up the process of bringing extinct species back to life. The platform leverages advanced 3D morphology, comparative genomics, and developmental biology to pinpoint genes that can be edited for de-extinction efforts, particularly when limited genomic data is available.

The company is currently using GenoMorph in its mission to resurrect the dodo bird. Unlike the woolly mammoth de-extinction project, which benefits from over 100 genomes due to better DNA preservation in cold climates, the dodo project faces challenges with only a single available genome from its tropical habitat.

GenoMorph was developed by collecting developmental data from various bird species, including chickens, quail, ducks, and pigeons, and combining it with genetic information and skull measurements from over 70 species. This year-long effort allows the AI to learn which DNA regions are active during beak and facial structure development, predicting key genetic switches for the dodo's iconic appearance.

The AI acts as a 'treasure map' for the dodo genome, guiding researchers to the most promising DNA editing targets. Colossal has already identified approximately 2,300 potential targets for the dodo's cranial facial morphology, which will now be tested in the lab. This addresses a major bottleneck in de-extinction: identifying the genetic changes that define a species.

To facilitate rapid testing of genetic edits, Colossal has also developed a system using lipid nanoparticles to deliver gene-editing tools directly into developing bird embryos. This method bypasses the need to wait for birds to reach sexual maturity, allowing for quicker validation of how specific genetic changes impact development.

In parallel, Colossal announced its Nicobar pigeon colony has grown to 36 birds, and they have successfully created the essential cells that develop into eggs and sperm. As the Nicobar pigeon is the dodo's closest living relative, these cells are crucial for introducing dodo traits into future birds.

Colossal CEO Ben Lamm emphasized that GenoMorph enhances the precision, control, and testability of genetic engineering. The platform identifies potential edits but does not introduce them directly, ensuring that decisions about genetic modification are informed and validated through rigorous testing.

The company's work has garnered support, with XPRIZE founder Peter Diamandis announcing a new VC firm, NeoGenesis Capital, to invest in companies utilizing Colossal Biosciences' programmable biology platform across various sectors including health, agriculture, and conservation.
